subject: Automotive & EVs
title: China's Battery Dominance
description: A short lesson to help you apply China's Battery Dominance.

hook.text: China controls over 75 percent of the world's battery cell manufacturing capacity.

buildup.text: CATL and BYD alone produce more cells than all of Europe, Japan, and the US combined.

discovery.text: China invested early and heavily in the entire supply chain—mining, refining, cell making, and recycling.

twist.text: Western governments are now scrambling to build domestic factories to reduce dependence on Chinese supply.

climax.text: The US Inflation Reduction Act pours billions into local battery plants, but catching China will take years.

punchline.text: Whoever makes the batteries controls the future of cars.

quiz.question: What share of global battery cell production does China control?

details.summary: China dominates the global EV battery supply chain, controlling most lithium processing, cell manufacturing, and pack assembly through companies like CATL and BYD that lead global market share.
details.whyItMatters: China's battery dominance has massive geopolitical implications. Western nations are investing billions to build domestic supply chains and reduce dependence on a single country for a critical technology.
takeaways: CATL and BYD are the world's largest battery manufacturers
China processes the majority of the world's lithium and cobalt
The US and EU are building gigafactories to reduce reliance on China

faq.question: How did China achieve such dominance in EV batteries?
faq.answer: China invested heavily in battery technology early, controlled critical mineral processing, subsidized domestic EV adoption to create demand, and built massive factory capacity that now supplies the world.

faq.question: Can Western countries catch up to China in battery production?
faq.answer: The US and EU are investing in domestic gigafactories and mineral processing. However, China's head start in scale, supply chains, and expertise means catching up will take years of sustained investment.
